name: Christopher Kelk Ingold
summary: British chemist and founder of physical organic chemistry.

name: University College London
summary: Major international centre for chemistry where Ingold served as Head of Department.

name: Imperial College London
summary: Institution where Ingold studied and worked early in his career.

name: University of Leeds
summary: University where Ingold was Professor of Organic Chemistry for six years.

name: Hartley University College
summary: College in Southampton where Ingold began tertiary education.

name: Cassell Cyanide Company
summary: Company where Ingold worked under the War Office and as a research chemist.

name: Institute of Chemistry
summary: Professional body where Ingold qualified as an Associate and Fellow.

name: Royal Society
summary: Scientific academy to which Ingold was elected Fellow.

name: Frederick George Donnan
summary: Physical chemist and Head of Department at UCL preceding Ingold.

name: Jocelyn Field Thorpe
summary: Chemist at Imperial College with whom Ingold worked.

name: E. D. Hughes
summary: Ingold's long-time collaborator who handled routine administrative tasks.

name: Kathleen Lonsdale
summary: Physicist and crystallographer recruited by Ingold to UCL.

name: Ronald Nyholm
summary: Inorganic chemist recruited back to UCL as a Professor.

name: Imperial Chemical Industries
summary: Chemical company that funded research at UCL until 1936.

name: University of London
summary: University granting degrees to UCL students and Ingold.

name: Christopher Ingold Laboratories
summary: New chemistry building at UCL opened in 1970.

name: Meldola Medal
summary: Award for a promising young scientist received by Ingold.

name: University of East Anglia
summary: University to which Ingold gave advice on departmental organization.

name: University of Ibadan
summary: University in Nigeria where Ingold delivered a lecture on scientific education.
